source.title: ChatGPT is adding real cartoonists' signatures to fake New Yorker cartoons
source.author: rdmuser

title.zh: ChatGPT签名争议：AI漫画冒用画家署名
title.en: ChatGPT Signatures Put Cartoonists at Risk

excerpt.zh: ChatGPT签名争议显示，AI生成的《纽约客》风格漫画可能附上真实漫画家的笔名。OpenAI虽更新了提示拦截，误归属问题仍未解决。
excerpt.en: The ChatGPT signatures controversy shows how AI-generated New Yorker-style cartoons can carry real artists' names, even after OpenAI added a warning.

disclosure.zh: 本文使用星期天AI中转站大模型，基于 Hacker News 内容自动生成。
disclosure.en: This article was automatically generated by the Weekly Day AI gateway model using content from Hacker News.

text.zh: ChatGPT签名让虚构漫画看似有真实作者
text.en: ChatGPT signatures make fictional cartoons look authorial

text.zh: ChatGPT签名争议源于一类由聊天机器人生成的《纽约客》风格单幅漫画：画面模仿该杂志的黑白线稿和讽刺文字，却在角落附上真实漫画家的笔名。漫画家布伦丹·洛珀发现，署名“BLOPER”的作品并非出自自己之手，却已在社交平台传播并引发读者询问。
text.en: The ChatGPT signatures controversy centers on a type of single-panel cartoon generated in The New Yorker's style. The images imitate the magazine's black-and-white line work and sardonic captions, while adding the pen names of real cartoonists. Brendan Loper discovered that a widely shared image bearing his signature, “BLOPER,” was not his work, yet readers contacted him as if it were.

text.zh: 署名不是普通装饰，而是身份与出处标记
text.en: A signature is an identity and provenance marker

text.zh: 报道记录了超过15名《纽约客》漫画家的署名出现在相关输出中，其中包括艾米莉·弗莱克、乔·戴特和帕特·伯恩斯等。漫画家认为，模仿风格与复制署名并不等价：风格相似可能引发版权讨论，而署名直接暗示作品经过本人创作或认可。对依靠署名确认作者、抵御脱离语境转载的插画而言，这会造成误导，也可能损害个人品牌。
text.en: The report documented signatures associated with more than 15 New Yorker cartoonists, including Emily Flake, Joe Dator, and Pat Byrnes. The artists distinguish style imitation from signature reproduction. A similar style may raise a copyright question, but a signature directly suggests that the work was created or endorsed by that person. For illustrators who rely on signatures to establish authorship amid context-free online reposting, the result can mislead audiences and damage a personal brand.

text.zh: OpenAI已加警告，但来源与责任仍不明
text.en: OpenAI added a warning, but the source and responsibility remain unclear

text.zh: OpenAI表示这是需要修复的非预期行为；在收到报道方通知后，ChatGPT开始对“纽约客风格”提示显示可能触及第三方相似性防护。不过，报道发布时，系统仍会给部分通用漫画加上真实漫画家的名字，说明防护并不稳定。另一个未解问题是模型如何获得这些署名：康泰纳仕与OpenAI的授权协议条款未公开，《纽约客》称从未授权开发者用其漫画训练模型，而公开资料也无法在报道范围内证明具体来源。
text.en: OpenAI said the behavior was unintended and should be addressed. After being notified by the reporter, ChatGPT began warning that requests for New Yorker-style cartoons might violate safeguards concerning similarity to third-party content. At publication, however, the system still attached real cartoonists' names to some generic images, showing that the protection was inconsistent. The source of the signatures also remains unresolved: the Condé Nast deal with OpenAI is not public, The New Yorker says it never authorized training on its cartoons, and the available reporting does not establish a specific ingestion path.

text.zh: 这起事件的核心不只是“AI画得像不像”，而是生成内容是否把不存在的作者关系包装成事实。美国现行知识产权规则尚未充分应对生成式图像中的署名冒用，版权、虚假归属和平台防护之间如何划界仍待明确。对新闻机构、平台和模型开发者而言，减少风格模仿只是一步；更重要的是避免把真实姓名或笔名附着到未经授权、未经本人认可的作品上，并为受影响的创作者提供可核查的申诉渠道。
text.en: The central issue is not only whether AI can draw similarly, but whether generated content presents a nonexistent author relationship as fact. U.S. intellectual-property law has not fully caught up with signature impersonation in generative images, leaving the boundaries among copyright, false attribution, and platform safeguards unsettled. For publishers, platforms, and model developers, limiting style imitation is only one step. They also need to prevent real names or pen names from being attached to unauthorized work and provide affected creators with a verifiable way to challenge such outputs.
